what_happened: Re-reading the monotonic-max clamp (scripts/lib/status-vocabulary.sh) showed task 304's recorded reasoning ('monotonic-max machinery prevents a later demotion by construction') does not mechanically hold: the clamp is opt-in, update-task-status.sh has no terminal-state guard on postflight writes, and 'partial' is deliberately unranked so status_vocabulary_would_regress(completed,partial) is false even when the clamp is applied. This let research recommend a concrete, low-risk Option (b) design reusing the already-proven partial-arm call shape, rather than treating the demotion as structurally blocked.

The dispatch's literal exit-code list for the commit-failure trigger (2/3/4/5/6, copied from WORK (i)'s existing ERROR-grouping case arm) includes exit 6, but git-staging-scope.md's own V9 semantics document exit 6 as 'the valid paths already committed successfully' -- i.e. not a genuine commit-landing failure. Recommended narrowing the status-demotion trigger set to {2,3,4,5} in the research report rather than reusing the dispatch's literal grouping unexamined; flagged as a decision for the plan phase to make deliberately.
